title: Birth, and a grandfather who played French horn
summary: Hug gives his birth date, and talks about his horn-playing grandfather's link to the Christian family.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Well Dick, I was born on Tulane Avenue, the exact address I don't know. I was born somewhere on Tulane. I was born December the 6th, 1910.
So, were your family musical at all?

Well, to some extent, yes. My grandfather on my mother's side, his name was Schmidt. My name being Hug, family name. My mother's family name was Schmidt. My grandfather played French horn. My grandfather played French horn. And he traveled around with circus bands. In fact, he was hardly ever at home. Grandmother hardly ever got to see him. I understand that he did play with the Christians at one time. To what extent, I just don't know. But I know that the Christian family were neighbors of my grandmother and my grandfather. In fact, Frankie Christian lived right next door to them. Frankie, I believe, was the one that was scheduled to go away with the original Dixon Land Band, wasn't he? I don't know.
I never could get that story.

I don't know. I better not make that statement because I'm not sure. But it seemed that I'd heard that. Frankie came to a sudden end. He died quite young. And I guess that probably was the reason why he may not have gone. I'm not sure about that. But that was the connection of my grandfather and the Christian family. And on my father's side, Jasper Hug, my uncle played drums. He played around in the old Waterville shows in town, the old suburban houses. And, well, my uncle was a Waterville entertainer. He played a little piano. My mother's brother. So, I don't know. I think that about covers the musical background. Outside of my mother, she played a little piano too.
